data.bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (unbounded secondary-device-type count copied into fixed 128-byte field)
data.rationale: p2p_group_info_parse() reads the Number of Secondary Device Types byte (u8) from each P2P Client Info Descriptor in the Group Info attribute and only validates it against the remaining descriptor bytes: 'if (8 * len > cend - g) return -1;' (p2p_parse.c:674). Since the descriptor length byte is limited to 255, len can still be up to 28, i.e. far above the 16 types (128 bytes) that the destination supports. cli->num_sec_dev_types and cli->sec_dev_types are then handed to p2p_copy_client_info() (p2p.c:453-457), which does os_memcpy(dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list, cli->sec_dev_types, 8 * cli->num_sec_dev_types) into the fixed u8 wps_sec_dev_type_list[WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN=128] field inside the heap-allocated struct p2p_device. The missing cap on len (should be limited so 8*len <= 128) lets up to ~224 bytes be written, corrupting subsequent fields of the heap p2p_device object (e.g. info.p2ps_instance pointer). Reachability from the fuzz target: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> p2p_scan_res_handler/p2p_probe_req_rx/p2p_rx_action -> p2p_add_device() -> p2p_add_group_clients() -> p2p_copy_client_info(). The corruption is intra-object so ASan does not flag the copy itself; it surfaces as a SEGV at free time (wpabuf_free via p2p_device_free), which was reproduced with an input carrying a WPS vendor IE, P2P attribute 0x0d (Device Info) and a Group Info attribute (0x0e) with a client descriptor declaring 20 secondary device types.
